title: Every Cut Grows Three
story: Thornabel the Gate Bramble has sealed the orphanage gate with 40 thick vines. Mr 6 learns the cruel rule: each time he slices one vine away, 3 new vines sprout in the very same second — but the bramble can only manage that trick 12 times before its sap runs dry.
question: After Mr 6 makes 12 cuts, each removing 1 vine but growing 3 back, how many vines block the gate?
hint: Each cut takes 1 away and adds 3 — so what is the NET change to the vine count per cut?
victory: Mr 6 stopped mid-swing, did the arithmetic, and cut exactly zero vines — instead he tickled Thornabel's roots until it untangled itself laughing. The orphans poured out through a gate of nothing but flowers.
imagePrompt: A numeral-six knight lowering his sword thoughtfully before a massive writhing bramble gate wound over an orphanage door, thorny vines glinting in warm afternoon light.
